prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: original diffuse material atlas for the native 3D Basilisco in Caelum Argenteum (#738), guided by the owned supplied reference. The input image is only a material/color reference, not a target to alter or reproduce as a flat character.
Create one opaque landscape 3-column by 2-row texture atlas. Six equal rectangular tiles fill the canvas with hard exact grid boundaries and no borders, text, gaps, labels or background outside the tiles. Each tile is a straight-on, evenly lit close material surface, subtle physically plausible detail, no cast shadows, lighting gradients, outlines, objects or recognizable creature silhouette. The material scale must be fine enough to wrap a small game creature without gigantic single scales.
Top left: dense overlapping small dark forest-green reptilian scales with subdued warm brass edges, following the creature's torso and tail.
Top middle: small overlapping copper/ochre abdominal scutes, warm brown-gold rather than bright metal.
Top right: dense fine russet/copper feathers with narrow darker shafts; oriented vertically from upper roots toward lower tips, referencing neck and wing feather colors.
Bottom left: deep natural crimson rooster comb and wattle skin, fine organic pebbled texture, no veins or gore.
Bottom middle: warm ochre/golden horn keratin, fine subtle lengthwise grain, for beak and leg details.
Bottom right: near-black charcoal claw keratin with restrained brown-gray lengthwise grain and enough detail to read in a game.
Preserve the original reference's muted green/copper/red/ochre/charcoal palette. This atlas contains only painted diffuse materials; the head, comb, feathers, wings, claws and curved tail will be actual closed geometry. No normal-map colors, no photo montage, no specular glare, no watermark.
